question: What are some effective drills I can do outdoors to improve my skills?
answer:

**Shooting (your 38% three-point mark is solid — keep building consistency)**
- **Catch-and-shoot from all 5 spots** (corners, wings, top): 10 reps per spot, alternating feet. You already do Sunday 9 AM shooting drills, so this slots in naturally.
- **Pull-up threes off a dribble**: 1-2 dribbles, then shoot. This feeds directly into the pick-and-roll focus you picked up after watching the Warriors–Suns game.
- **Off-the-glass bank shots**: 15 reps from the free-throw line. Good for building touch on a colder morning when the ball feels stiff.

**Lateral Quickness (you're up 18% since March — push the 3-cone time)**
- **3-cone drill** (your 10-second target, currently 11.5s): Set cones 10 ft apart, shuffle laterally, then sprint back. Do 6–8 reps with 30s rest. This is your existing drill, so keep logging times.
- **Ladder + cone combo**: Lateral shuffles through a 4-rung ladder, then a 5-yard sprint to a cone. Repeat 5x each direction. Builds the footwork speed that feeds into the quickness you've gained.
- **Defensive slide + closeout**: Slide laterally for 10 seconds, then sprint 5 yards to "close out" on a spot. Do 6 reps. This mirrors what you're teaching the youth team on defense.

**Dribbling (you're already doing 4×30-min sessions/week — add variety)**
- **Crossover + between-the-legs + behind-the-back combo**: 30 seconds each direction, 4 sets. Keep it at game speed, not slow.
- **Dribble-and-shoot off a screen**: Dribble to the wing, "screen" off a cone, then pull up for a mid-range jumper. 8 reps per side. This bridges dribbling into your pick-and-roll work.
- **One-hand dribble while walking/running**: 2 minutes each hand. Builds the loose, relaxed touch that helps in open-court pickup games.

**Pick-and-Roll Specific (your stated focus)**
- **P&R read drill**: Dribble to the top, pass to a "screener" (cone), then cut to the basket. Alternate: shoot the pull-up, kick out, or drive. 10 reps, then switch roles. Do this with Corey at your Saturday pickup — he's been your partner since 2021, so he can fill the screener role.
- **Short-roll vs. long-roll**: Same setup, but emphasize the timing difference. Short roll = quick hit to the rim; long roll = catch at the elbow and shoot. 5 reps each.

**How to fit it in**
Your 8–10 AM outdoor window is your best slot. A 45-minute session could look like: 10 min warm-up (ladder + dynamic stretches), 15 min shooting, 10 min quickness/cones, 10 min dribbling or P&R. You don't need to hit everything every day — rotate shooting and quickness days, and save P&R work for when you can get Corey or another partner.

One caveat: you're already logging a lot of hours (60 in July, 65 in September, 70 in October, 80 in December). If you add more outdoor sessions, make sure you're not cutting into recovery — your ice baths, stretching, and yoga are doing real work.
